      "body": "The resource still routes PATCH /admin/groups/:id to this action, but the previously supported changes.add and changes.delete payloads are now ignored. An existing membership-removal request returns success while leaving the user in the group, potentially retaining access that the caller intended to revoke. Because that request does not include visible, it also unexpectedly hides the group. Preserve the PATCH contract or explicitly reject incompatible requests rather than silently succeeding."
    },

      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6",

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Provide pagination for the public member list",
      "body": "Group.findMembers now requests only 50 members and replaces the members collection with that page. This public route calls it once, and the public members template has no pagination or load-more controls. Consequently, members beyond the first 50 are unreachable in the public UI; non-automatic groups previously displayed their complete membership. Add public pagination or load the remaining pages."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6",
      "line": 13,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Avoid adding an empty page for exact multiples of the page size",
      "body": "Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts pages whenever the membership count is an exact multiple of the limit. For a group with 50 members and a limit of 50, the UI displays two pages and enables Next, which requests offset 50 and displays an empty member list. Use ceiling division for the page count."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Do not fetch membership using an unsaved group name",
      "body": "The editable name field is two-way-bound to the group's name. After an administrator changes it without saving, pagination and the refresh following addMembers or removeMember fetch membership using that unsaved name, while the membership mutation still targets the original group ID. The refresh therefore fails with a missing group or displays another group's members if the proposed name already exists. Use a persisted identifier or persisted name until the rename succeeds."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js",
      "line": 31,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Prevent stale member requests from overwriting newer pages",
      "body": "Every findMembers response unconditionally replaces both offset and members, while the navigation actions allow another request before the previous one completes. Clicking Next twice can issue requests for offsets 50 and 100; if the offset-100 response arrives first, the slower offset-50 response then moves the UI back to the older page. Serialize navigation requests or ignore responses that no longer correspond to the latest request."
    }

findings.title: Preserve or explicitly reject PATCH membership updates
findings.body: The resource still routes PATCH /admin/groups/:id to this action, but the previously supported changes.add and changes.delete payloads are now ignored. An existing membership-removal request returns success while leaving the user in the group, potentially retaining access that the caller intended to revoke. Because that request does not include visible, it also unexpectedly hides the group. Preserve the PATCH contract or explicitly reject incompatible requests rather than silently succeeding.

findings.title: Provide pagination for the public member list
findings.body: Group.findMembers now requests only 50 members and replaces the members collection with that page. This public route calls it once, and the public members template has no pagination or load-more controls. Consequently, members beyond the first 50 are unreachable in the public UI; non-automatic groups previously displayed their complete membership. Add public pagination or load the remaining pages.

findings.title: Avoid adding an empty page for exact multiples of the page size
findings.body: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts pages whenever the membership count is an exact multiple of the limit. For a group with 50 members and a limit of 50, the UI displays two pages and enables Next, which requests offset 50 and displays an empty member list. Use ceiling division for the page count.

findings.title: Do not fetch membership using an unsaved group name
findings.body: The editable name field is two-way-bound to the group's name. After an administrator changes it without saving, pagination and the refresh following addMembers or removeMember fetch membership using that unsaved name, while the membership mutation still targets the original group ID. The refresh therefore fails with a missing group or displays another group's members if the proposed name already exists. Use a persisted identifier or persisted name until the rename succeeds.

findings.title: Prevent stale member requests from overwriting newer pages
findings.body: Every findMembers response unconditionally replaces both offset and members, while the navigation actions allow another request before the previous one completes. Clicking Next twice can issue requests for offsets 50 and 100; if the offset-100 response arrives first, the slower offset-50 response then moves the UI back to the older page. Serialize navigation requests or ignore responses that no longer correspond to the latest request.
